data.narrative:
The Red Metal Company is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Jackson Switzer that has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of nine private companies in the climate and energy sector, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The stage-progression method, which applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yields an implied valuation of $25M when applied to the company's $10M raised as a proxy baseline. A peer-median approach could not be executed; while nine same-sector peers exist, insufficient overlap emerged in same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier subsets (fewer than three datapoints in each category), making a narrow peer multiple unreliable.

The triangulated valuation range is $21M to $29M, with a median of $25M. This range reflects±15% sensitivity around the single derived method. The primary uncertainty is methodological: reliance on stage-progression alone, without peer-multiple triangulation, limits confidence in calibration. A more robust valuation would require either tighter clustering of seed-stage climate-tech comparables at similar funding levels or earlier-stage transaction data from the peer set to validate the 2.5x step-up assumption specific to this sector and company profile.
